title: Tom Harris and his bass
summary: Dawson recalls bassist Tom Harris, who died soon after buying a new bass that Dawson later bought, and his Lincoln Beach band.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: You know, I used to go uptown to a place called... Thomas Beer Garden in 1945 and saw a bass player up there named Tom Harris. Remember that?

Yeah, Tom Harris. Yeah, Tom Harris. Well, he wasn't much. He wasn't that... I think that's the same bass that I've got now. It was brand new and he had been working out of Lincoln Beach. And the lady out there that was running Lincoln Beach, she stood for security for that bass. He bought that bass from White Island. It was brand new. And I don't believe he had it two years when he died, you see. After he died, then I bought it. His aunt.
Who was he playing out at Lincoln Beach with?
Nah, he got me. He had a band out there. I can't remember, but he had a pretty fair band out there. But he was playing with that band. I don't know who...
I know he used to play with Avery and Tillman uptown when I heard him up by the park. Yeah.
